reconcile.connective: Harmonizers separate the two notices: only Dathan and Abiram stood with their families when the earth opened, while Korah himself was elsewhere, so his sons survived.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the plain reading that Numbers 16 swallows Korah's whole household alive, which the later notice that 'the children of Korah died not' cannot stand beside.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, contradiction "Did God bury alive all of Korah's children?"
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Korah being a Kohathite, his tent could not have been in the Reubenite camp, and it does not appear that he himself was on the spot where Dathan and Abiram stood with their families.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly carries the central harmonization: Korah was not present where the swallowed families stood, so the household swallowed in Num 16 was Dathan's and Abiram's, leaving room for Korah's sons to survive (Num 26:11).

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871), on Numbers 16:27 and 26:11
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: JFB treats this exact tension, arguing Korah was not on the spot where Dathan and Abiram stood with their families and that his children 'died not' because they withdrew from the rebellion.
